The course is very, very dependent on your instructor. Two people who take ENG 101 from two distinct instructors could have polar opposite feelings at the end of the term. If you somehow end up with a bad instructor, the course might become an absolute nightmare, especially considering the high thresholds for letter grades. Donna Moros changes an otherwise extremely dull course to an engaging one. She is very enjoyable to listen to because of her range of interests and her great personality. Her relationship with students is perfect. There is an effortless mutual respect when Donna Moros is in the room. What strikes to me the most is she never judges opinions when collecting ideas, she is always on inspiring side when disagreements arise, and that immediately makes everyone more talkative or at least enjoy a better class environment than other sections. She is always helpful, she connects to her students on individual level when needed. She is a great observer, conducts the course topic greatly, she has an understanding of her students and call them by their names within first weeks. She made everything about the course very clear several times, like assignments, grading system and deadlines. Bilkent is better with likes of Ms Moros.

The only weak point of the course was her theme. She is a very lovely teacher and professional at her job. She makes sure everybody understands what is expected from the assignments throughout the course. She was also very tolerant and generous in terms of points.

course: Course is good for academic english

This course has severe problems. Firstly, as a speaker of 4 languages, I do not want to invest my time and energy on an English writing course. Especially with such a punishing attendance limit. For example, my former university Boğaziçi does not have such a course in any of their undergraduate programs. It is mandatory only for the students who passed their proficiency on the lower end(as a forced elective). 7 hour max is laughable for such little course content. I could do in this course just as well only by following what's on moodle. Even with a god-send instructor like Donna Moros and nice classmates, my friends also made fun of this class and tried to focus on positives. This class was also a bit like "learn about different things and have more critical thinking". Bilkent has the fundamental problem of seeing their students as teenagers in its many organs(unlike Boğaziçi) when universities are open to anyone. I have qualification in English and I came here to become and engineer, so I want to learn about engineering. University should educate someone in different fields and socializing with its environment but not with ---MANDATORY--- courses Iike this. I am having a history class (IR311-Russian History) this semester where our professor asked how many languages we spoke in the first course, and our ENG class topic was about history but in a very very different level in comparison with IR331. It felt like the bug of a system when I went from one class to the other. This is part of the reasons why Bilkent is worse than Boğaziçi because it is a different mentality to treat students as adults.

As an engineering student, this course takes too much time and effort. I don't think this course should stand out as one of the most critical courses in the semester. Reducing the workload would be great.
